summary: The agent implemented most of the configurable collection feature and preserved all baseline behavior, but failed two hidden tests because direct collection and map bean-property copies invoked configured implementations with an unsupported copy-constructor argument instead of constructing them with source size or the no-argument constructor.
quick_failure_summary: Configured implementations fail to compile for direct collection and map bean-property copies.

details.reasoning: The new suite ran 53 tests, with 51 passing and both compiler variants of shouldUseConfiguredConstructionForDirectCollectionProperties failing. The agent replaced TypeFactory's implementation entries globally, but did not update CollectionAssignmentBuilder and NewInstanceSetterWrapperForCollectionsAndMaps for configured direct assignments. Generated code therefore attempted forms such as new PropertyList<>(sourceCollection), although the validated configured classes only expose no-argument and optional int constructors. The reference solution explicitly marks configured implementation types and routes direct assignments through the new-instance setter wrapper, passing source.size() only when the int constructor is usable.
details.secondary_factors: The agent added a bean-copy test, but its mapper also declared copyList and copyMap mapping methods. Those methods masked the direct-assignment path, so the focused tests passed without exercising the explicitly required case that later failed.

justification.issue_description: Direct List, Map, and Set values copied into bean properties were not constructed according to the configured implementation constructor rules.
justification.evidence: The prompt explicitly states: 'The rule applies to every mapping form, including collection or map values copied directly into bean properties' and requires using source size for a usable public int constructor. The visible processor code contains the direct-assignment decision in CollectionAssignmentBuilder and construction template in NewInstanceSetterWrapperForCollectionsAndMaps.ftl. The agent did not modify those files, while the reference solution does.
justification.verdict_reasoning: FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT is appropriate because this mapping form and its constructor behavior were explicit in the prompt and the relevant construction path was discoverable in the repository. The hidden test did not introduce an undocumented convention; it directly exercised the stated requirement.

problem_assessment.notes: This is a broad annotation-processor feature involving classpath resource loading, Java properties parsing, type-system validation, processing rounds, constructor selection, factories, and several code-generation paths. The failing direct-property requirement was nevertheless stated unambiguously, and the reference solution demonstrates that the task is solvable.

evidence: JUnit reports 3641 of 3641 baseline tests passing and 51 of 53 new tests passing.
Both failures occur while compiling generated PropertyCollectionMapper code and report constructor argument/type-inference errors for PropertyList, PropertyMap, and PropertySet.
The agent successfully ran 65 focused tests and Checkstyle in the trajectory; there were no dependency, runtime, API, or test-bootstrap failures.

An initial overly broad find command encountered unrelated permission warnings, but the agent interrupted it and immediately continued with /app-scoped commands, so it did not materially block the work.

The post-agent harness noted a three-way test.patch merge failure, then reset the affected test files, reapplied the harness, and successfully executed all 3699 classified tests; this did not cause the two feature-specific failures.
environment_assessment.finding: No meaningful external blocker was found; the failures are isolated to an omitted direct-property construction path in the implementation.
